answer_1.quote: We task GPT-4 to (i) define a set of pseudofunctions that suffice to execute the protocol, and (ii) convert the protocol steps into pseudocode using only the provided pseudofunctions.

answer_2.quote: We report precision and recall of function calls, use the normalized Levenshtein distance to measure ordering, compute SciBERTScore and BLEU for argument values, and also report function‑level precision/recall.

answer_3.quote: We use GPT-4 as an evaluator, where given (i) a protocol description, (ii) admissible pseudofunctions, (iii) ground‑truth pseudocode, (iv) predicted pseudocode, the model is prompted to predict which one of (iii) or (iv) better matches the protocol description.
methods: pairwise evaluation (choose better of ground‑truth vs. model output)

answer_4.quote: We worked with an undergraduate biomedical sciences student and asked them to complete the next step prediction task and the function selection task. Human Precision was 87.5%, and human accuracy was 54.8% (n=32).
answer_4.guideline: Participants were asked to select the correct next step or the correct set of functions for a given protocol description.
